ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Mr. Zhang drinks the wine while Mr. Li becomes drunk: the proverb marks a mismatch between actor and consequence.
EvidenceBody: Zhang performs the act of drinking, but Mr. Li bears its effect and gets drunk. The stock line occurs 125 times in 84 allowlisted texts. Masters use that observable mismatch as an answer to otherwise different public questions: why the monastery superintendent lost his eyebrows after Danxia burned the wooden buddha, what Yunmen Wenyan means, and why there is no buddha teaching at the start of a good year. The corpus extends the joke: “Mr. Li sobers up and questions Mr. Zhang, just making Mr. Zhang lose his good temper” (李公醉醒問張公，恰使張公無好氣). In a teaching-seat enumeration it stands beside “Zhong Kui can dance the eighteen beats, the golden cock sings dawn, and the stone woman roams in spring” (鍾馗解舞十八拍，金雞唱曉，石女游春). Lianyue Guangsi turns the mismatch back into a question: “since Mr. Zhang drank the wine, why is Mr. Li drunk?” (既是張公喫酒，因甚李公卻醉). Sixin Wuxin repeats the line, asks its import, and refuses to explain it: “Let the blue sea change as it may; in the end I will not explain it to you” (任從滄海變，終不為君通). Zen bends the comic actor/effect mismatch into a reusable interview answer, verse line, teaching-seat enumeration, and new public question. The records license that structural inference but do not equate the proverb with one universal hidden answer to every case.
